audit.why: Full-layer sides and content win[0..6] both read Zed on all seven rows and match the packet chart. Brand has no dash and no self-peel, so no stage flips to him.
Spikes are right: level 3 string, level 6 Death Mark (120/110/100s), first item, and a late game that stays Zed's because Brand never gains mobility. Brand's own spike is Sear reaching 6s at rank 5.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says 'Q only stuns when you are ablaze' but never names which spells apply Blaze, never gives Sear's cooldown, and never mentions that three Blaze stacks detonate on their own after 2 seconds — which is what actually catches Zed mid-mark.
audit.why: Riot's text: Blaze stacks to 3 and detonates in 2 seconds applying spell effects; Sear stuns only an ablaze target; Pillar of Flame deals 25% more to an ablaze target; Conflagration's spread doubles on an ablaze target. Every stun in this lane is set up by W or E landing first.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns field and the Don'ts now state Sear at 8s/6s, Conflagration at 13s, and the 2-second detonation.

audit.why: The kit gives Sear 8/7.5/7/6.5/6, Pillar of Flame 10/9.5/9/8.5/8, Conflagration 13/12/11/10/9, Pyroclasm 100/90/80, and Living Shadow 20/19/18/17/16.

audit.why: Lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED plus the template sweep.
audit.corrected: All four bodies rewritten to their titles and grounded in Brand's Blaze mechanics.

edits.before: - Brand Sear (Stun): matchup-defining — Q only stuns when you are ablaze — after eating W or E, the stun line is the dodge that matters. It governs your forward steps. - W Living Shadow (swap) spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Sear is 8s at rank 1 and 6s maxed, and it only stuns while you are ablaze — dodge the line after his Pillar of Flame or Conflagration lands. - Conflagration is 13s at rank 1: that gap is your step-in. - Your W Living Shadow is 20s, so never spend the swap on poke.

notes: The kit file tags Brand's W Pillar of Flame with a 'terrain' flag; Riot's own description says it is a delayed area of magic damage and creates no terrain, so I treated the flag as a tooltip-parsing misfire and wrote nothing about walls or blocked dashes. Chart was already consistent across both layers and matched the packet, so no chart edits. breakdown.wave and breakdown.early remain structurally templated — nothing in Brand's kit gave me a wave-specific hook I could ground without inventing.
